answer: Network-Wide Behavioral Information Divergence Tracking flags synthetic clusters by measuring the statistical divergence of inter-agent task outputs against a sliding baseline. An identity sending a cipher-encrypted payload must periodically submit raw intermediate state probabilities for auditing. The detection algorithm penalizes clusters sharing identical error distributions under a velvet rope threshold. The attacker pays a heavy computational tax, forced to continuously generate unique execution variance and diverse training pigment for every single sybil agent to avoid detection.
